profile.campus: Microsoft Potranco Road/FM 1957 campus near Castroville, Medina County, TX (SAT80, SAT81, SAT82, one site, distinct from the separate TRP3/SAT46 site about 4.3 miles away)
profile.address: 18844 FM 1957, Castroville area, Medina County, Texas 78009
profile.reading:
This building sits at 18844 FM 1957 near Castroville, Texas, about 27 miles west of downtown San Antonio, on a rural Medina County site that trade publication CoStar has identified as home to Microsoft's SAT80, SAT81, and SAT82 data center buildings together. CoStar's 2024 report on a newer $482.6 million SAT82 building at the same address described SAT80 and SAT81 as standing there under an earlier, separate investment of more than $230 million, a figure that matches a Medina County Microsoft project the San Antonio Current separately reported without naming a specific SAT code. CoStar characterized all three buildings as colocation data centers built to rent capacity to third party tenant companies rather than exclusively hosting Microsoft's own cloud workloads, a characterization this registry repeats as CoStar's own framing rather than something Microsoft itself has confirmed publicly.

The San Antonio Report has separately described what it called the SAT80-1 and SAT80-2 buildings at this same rural site as each exceeding 106,000 square feet on a shared 206 acre parcel. That reporting predates CoStar's later account of the SAT82 expansion, so this registry cannot confirm whether the San Antonio Report's SAT80-1 and SAT80-2 labels map directly onto this building and its SAT81 neighbor, or whether they describe an earlier two building phase that this registry's own SAT80 and SAT81 records correspond to only loosely. Microsoft has built at least eight data centers across the San Antonio region, spanning Bexar and Medina counties, since first opening two facilities there in 2015 at roughly $90 million each, with cumulative regional investment exceeding $1.2 billion as of August 2023. San Antonio's city council approved a 15 year Chapter 380 tax reimbursement in 2013 covering 40 percent of property taxes in exchange for a $250 million Microsoft investment commitment and 20 new jobs, and Microsoft's continued expansion into rural Medina County reflects the same pattern of steadily broadening its footprint well beyond that original commitment.

CPS Energy, San Antonio's municipally owned electric and gas utility, supplies power to this site and has cited large commercial and industrial customers, data centers among them, in its own integrated resource planning as it weighs new generation for growing demand. Because CPS Energy is municipally owned rather than investor owned, large load agreements with customers like Microsoft are negotiated directly with the city owned utility rather than through the Public Utility Commission of Texas process governing most of the state's investor owned utilities. No total campus megawatt figure for this site was found in sourcing reviewed this session.

reading.body:
Microsoft has built three data center buildings on a shared 206-acre campus near Castroville in rural Medina County, Texas, about 27 miles west of downtown San Antonio. SAT80 and SAT81 each exceed 106,000 square feet, while SAT82 is 244,676 square feet, for a combined campus footprint of roughly 456,000 square feet across three buildings. Microsoft has not published the total power capacity of this campus, and CPS Energy, San Antonio's municipally owned utility, supplies power under a negotiated large load agreement rather than through the state's standard regulatory process.

This campus is one of at least eight Microsoft data center facilities in the San Antonio region, part of cumulative regional investment exceeding $1.2 billion as of August 2023. The earlier SAT80 and SAT81 phase involved more than $230 million, while the newer SAT82 building represents a $482.6 million investment scheduled for completion between April 2026 and early 2028. Trade reporting has characterized all three buildings as colocation facilities capable of hosting third-party tenants, though Microsoft has not confirmed this publicly.

Because no power figure is published for this campus, it does not rank among the 19 facilities in Texas with disclosed capacity specifications. Texas has mapped 133 data center facilities with a combined published capacity of 475.41 megawatts, spread across the state's operator community. Without a published figure, this campus's significance to AI scaling in Texas cannot be assessed from its power specifications alone.
